name: libcxxabi

patches.reason: Confirmed for real (2026-08-22): the shared cxxabi_shared library link failed with 'undefined reference to `__dso_handle`' (referenced by cxa_thread_atexit.cpp's own __cxa_thread_atexit()). This project's own crt1.o never defines __dso_handle (Bionic's real crtbegin/crtend split is not imported) -- extra_files above already writes src/__crt_dso_handle.cpp (a tiny CRT-owned shim providing it) into the fetched checkout, matching the OLD (pre-migration) recipe's own identical extra_files entry, but the OLD recipe *also* had a patch wiring that file into LIBCXXABI_SOURCES (this new source's own set(LIBCXXABI_SOURCES ...) list, confirmed by reading the fetched file, does not reference it at all) -- without which the shim is written to disk but never actually compiled or linked. Re-added here as a direct list insertion (simpler than the OLD patch's own 'insert before the LIBCXXABI_ENABLE_NEW_DELETE_DEFINITIONS conditional' approach, and unconditional -- __dso_handle is needed regardless of that option's value).

Confirmed for real (2026-08-22) on Windows: the shared libc++abi.dll link failed with `ld.lld: error: undefined symbol: _tls_index` (referenced by this file's own `static thread_local __cxa_eh_globals eh_globals;` in its __has_feature(cxx_thread_local) branch, confirmed by reading the fetched file directly). Clang always reports __has_feature(cxx_thread_local) as true (it is a language feature, not a platform capability), so this branch is taken on every target including Windows; on Windows PE, a real `thread_local` variable lowers to code that references the native _tls_index/_tls_used TLS-directory symbols, which are normally defined by a real CRT's tlssup.obj -- this project's own crt1.o has no such thing, since (confirmed by reading libc/src/tls.c and libc/include/private/crt_tls.h directly) this project implements its own TlsAlloc/TlsGetValue-based dynamic TLS instead of relying on compiler-native PE TLS anywhere else in the codebase. This file's own third (#else) branch already exists purely to serve platforms without a working `thread_local` (via std::__libcpp_tls_key, a portable pthread_key_create-shaped abstraction, confirmed by reading it) -- since LIBCXXABI_HAS_PTHREAD_API=ON/LIBCXX_HAS_PTHREAD_API=ON are already set for this project's own real pthread implementation (itself backed by the same TlsAlloc-based libc/src/tls.c), that fallback branch works correctly here and needs no further changes; only the branch selector itself needed excluding Windows. Scope-checked before patching: grepped the whole fetched libcxx/src and libcxxabi/src trees for `thread_local` -- this is the only file/line where it is a real, unconditional compiler-native `thread_local` variable declaration (the four other hits -- cxa_thread_atexit.cpp, thread.cpp, condition_variable.cpp, future.cpp -- are either comments or route through this project's own already-working __thread_specific_ptr/__libcpp_tls_key portable abstraction, not the raw keyword).

notes: cmake.install_component="cxxabi" (new, tools/crt-libcxx-build.py's own build_recipe() now reads this): required specifically because this recipe's own driver add_subdirectory()s libcxx alongside libcxxabi (see the driver's own comment) -- a plain `cmake --install <dir>` with no --component restriction installs *every* install() rule the combined CMake project graph knows about, including libcxx's own, and libcxx's own install rules reference files (e.g. libcxx.imp) only generated by libcxx targets this recipe deliberately never builds. Confirmed for real: `CMake Error ... file INSTALL cannot find .../libcxx.imp` the first time `cmake --install` ran unrestricted against this combined build tree. "cxxabi" matches the COMPONENT name libcxxabi's own fetched src/CMakeLists.txt already gives its install(TARGETS ... COMPONENT cxxabi) calls (confirmed directly, and confirmed sufficient on its own: a `cmake --install <dir> --component cxxabi` run by hand installed both the shared and static libc++abi artifacts and nothing from libcxx at all).

2026-08-22: MIGRATED off the old source.repository (platform/external/libcxxabi) to toolchain/llvm-project's own libcxxabi/ subtree, in lockstep with ../libcxx/recipe.json's own identical migration -- see that file's own notes for the full reasoning (the old platform/external/libcxx* Android forks are confirmed dead, frozen since a 2024-12-20 placeholder "Empty merge" commit, which is why libcxx's own C++20 <bit> support was missing entirely). source.ref reuses the exact same pinned commit as ../libcxx and ../libunwind's own recipe.json (37f38d1f3276b62fba09462ab4807dce846c732d) -- all three now describe one single, consistent monorepo snapshot.

source.sparse_paths now also includes libcxx (not just libcxxabi/cmake/runtimes/cmake): the fetched libcxxabi/CMakeLists.txt defaults LIBCXXABI_LIBCXX_PATH to "${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/../libcxx" (confirmed by reading the fetched file) -- with both recipes' own checkout_subdir landing as true siblings under the shared source root (source_root/libcxx, source_root/libcxxabi, exactly matching tools/crt-libcxx-build.py's own source_root / recipe['name'] layout), this relative default resolves correctly on its own. The explicit LLVM_EXTERNAL_LIBCXX_SOURCE_DIR override below is kept anyway rather than relying on that default silently working, matching this recipe's own pre-existing conservative style.

cmake.driver (new): the fetched libcxxabi/CMakeLists.txt at this commit, like ../libcxx's own, no longer calls project() itself (confirmed by grepping the full file for `^project(` -- zero matches) -- needs the same driver-CMakeLists.txt treatment as ../libunwind and ../libcxx now both use.

This recipe's own driver (libstdc++/third_party/libcxxabi/standalone/CMakeLists.txt) ALSO add_subdirectory()s libcxx alongside libcxxabi, unlike ../libunwind's own driver (which only ever add_subdirectory()s itself) -- see that driver file's own long comment for the full story, confirmed for real: libcxxabi/src/CMakeLists.txt does `target_link_libraries(cxxabi_shared_objects PRIVATE cxx-headers ...)` (and the same for cxxabi_static_objects), where "cxx-headers" is an INTERFACE target only libcxx/CMakeLists.txt itself defines (exposing libcxx's own CMake-generated __config_site, which cannot be worked around with a raw -I flag the way libunwind's own extra_checkout_dirs problem could be -- confirmed no plain, pre-generated __config_site is committed anywhere in the fetched source, only the __config_site.in template). This recipe's own cmake --build --target cxxabi build step (unchanged) never actually builds any of libcxx's own targets from this configure -- they exist only so "cxx-headers" (and nothing else libcxx-specific) is a real, resolvable target.

CRT_LIBCXX_SOURCE_DIR and the LIBCXX_* options duplicated here (ENABLE_SHARED/STATIC/EXCEPTIONS/RTTI/THREADS/HAS_PTHREAD_API/USE_COMPILER_RT/HAS_RT_LIB, plus the three INCLUDE_TESTS/BENCHMARKS/DOCS=OFF, plus LIBCXX_CXX_ABI/_INCLUDE_PATHS/_LIBRARY_PATH) intentionally mirror ../libcxx/recipe.json's own values exactly -- this bootstrap configure generates its own real, independent copy of libcxx's __config_site (consumed by libcxxabi's own compile via "cxx-headers", see the note above), and it must describe the exact same feature set (threading model, exceptions, etc.) that ../libcxx/recipe.json's own *separate* configure will also generate later for the real, installed libc++ headers -- a mismatch between the two would be a real, silent ABI/behavior inconsistency, not a cosmetic one. If ../libcxx/recipe.json's own feature-affecting options ever change, update this list to match.

LIBCXX_CXX_ABI=system-libcxxabi is set here too (not left at the in-tree "libcxxabi" default, even though cxxabi_shared/cxxabi_static genuinely do exist in this same combined configure once add_subdirectory() order is fixed -- see the driver's own comment). Confirmed for real this matters, not just for consistency with ../libcxx/recipe.json: libcxx/src/CMakeLists.txt's own add_custom_command evaluates `$<TARGET_PROPERTY:libcxx-abi-shared,IMPORTED_LIBNAME>` unconditionally, but the in-tree "libcxxabi" branch's own libcxx-abi-shared is a plain `add_library(... INTERFACE)` (no IMPORTED_LIBNAME property at all, since it is not created via import_shared_library()) -- untested here whether that resolves to an empty string harmlessly or fails a different way, and not worth finding out: "system-libcxxabi" builds libcxx-abi-shared via import_shared_library(), which does set IMPORTED_LIBNAME, exactly like ../libcxx/recipe.json's own already-working configuration.

add_subdirectory() order in the driver (libcxxabi first, then libcxx) matters and is not arbitrary: unlike target_link_libraries()'s forward-reference tolerance (see the "cxx-headers" note above), libcxx/CMakeLists.txt's own `include(HandleLibCXXABI)` does a real, immediately-evaluated `if (TARGET cxxabi_shared)` check, not a generate-time-deferred one. Confirmed for real: add_subdirectory()-ing libcxx before libcxxabi left cxxabi_shared not yet defined at the moment that check ran, surfacing later as `CMake Error ... Target "libcxx-abi-shared" not found` -- the exact same error class as the original "cxx-headers not found" problem this driver exists to fix, just from the opposite ordering mistake.

extra_checkout_dirs (cmake/, runtimes/cmake/): same reason and mechanism as ../libunwind and ../libcxx's own matching notes -- confirmed by reading the fetched libcxxabi/CMakeLists.txt's own CMAKE_MODULE_PATH references to "../cmake" and "../runtimes/cmake/Modules". Shared (not re-fetched) across all three recipes.

patches: started empty, not migrated blind -- same reasoning as ../libcxx/recipe.json's own matching note (the OLD recipe's four patches were all written against the old fork's exact file layout/line content, none assumed to still apply). One has since been rediscovered for real, the same way the originals were found (build, diagnose, fix, document): the __dso_handle wiring, now recorded in the patches array above -- this new source needed a real list-insertion patch again, not just the extra_files shim alone, though the exact insertion mechanism differs from the OLD patch's own approach (see that patch's own "reason" field). The other three OLD patches (MINGW_LIBRARIES no-op, _LIBCPP_BUILDING_LIBRARY define, RUNTIME DESTINATION install fix) have not been re-encountered yet -- Linux was reached first this migration; Windows may resurface some or all of them once attempted.

LIBCXXABI_USE_LLVM_UNWINDER=OFF is now explicit (the OLD recipe left it unset/implicit-OFF, relying on upstream's own then-default). Confirmed for real this had to change: the new source's own libcxxabi/CMakeLists.txt now defaults this option to ON and, when it is ON, hard-fails configure with `FATAL_ERROR: LIBCXXABI_USE_LLVM_UNWINDER is set to ON, but libunwind is not specified in LLVM_ENABLE_RUNTIMES` -- LLVM_ENABLE_RUNTIMES is a combined-single-CMake-project "runtimes" build variable this project's own separate-recipe-per-component driver never sets (and does not want to: see the reasoning immediately below, unchanged from the OLD recipe). Explicitly forcing this OFF avoids the whole check and keeps libcxxabi compiling against the plain, portable Itanium _Unwind_* ABI surface -- exactly what this project's own from-source libunwind already exports, so nothing is actually lost.

LIBCXXABI_LIBUNWIND_INCLUDES: deliberately still left unset, matching the OLD recipe's own note in full (a combined single-CMake-project "runtimes" build is what actually wires this automatically upstream, which this project's separate-recipe-per-component build does not have and does not want) -- that reasoning is about this project's own build architecture, not about which fork libcxxabi's source comes from, so it carries forward unchanged.
